conviction_note: The fundamental read leans negative: H1 cash generation was $14M ex-safe-harbor against a $200-375M full-year guide, so H2 must deliver $186-361M on subscriber additions about 30% below 2025, and Q3 capital costs rose. The setup leans the other way: 32% of the float is short with 8.75 days to cover, calls are bid by 28.5 vol points, and the sell side cut its bar through October. My findings sum to about -0.1 and p_up is 49 on a 17% absolute move. A known negative is set against a crowded short, and I could not say why the option market is wrong, so the sign stays close to a coin flip.
bar: Company guide (Aug 5 2026 8-K): FY2026 Cash Generation $200-375M excluding $50-100M of equipment safe-harbor investment (cut from $250-450M); FY2026 Aggregate Subscriber Value $4.6-4.9B (cut from $4.8-5.2B). No Q3-specific guide. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001469367/000162828026053349/exhibit991q226.htm . Street EPS/revenue is disputed and is not the line RUN trades on: Investing.com $0.16 / $760M (https://ph.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/sunrun-earnings-in-focus-as-borrowing-costs-test-solar-demand-93CH-2675272), MarketBeat $0.20 / $757.5M, Zacks $0.26 / $804.1M (via https://solarcomplaint.com/research/sunrun-q3-2026-earnings), Earnings Whispers $0.14 / $810M. I found no consensus for Q3 cash generation or ASV. print_vs_bar_pct is my read of Q3 ASV and cash generation against the run-rate the FY guide implies.
positioning_check: Short interest is 71.66M shares (previous 70.71M): 32.44% of float, 29.75% of shares outstanding, short ratio 8.75 days (stockanalysis.com statistics, page updated 2026-11-04, settlement date not shown; https://www.stockanalysis.com/stocks/run/statistics/). Investing.com on 2026-11-04 says about 35% of float is short. The baseline 25-delta skew is -28.53 vol points (calls bid, 'upside paid'), the put/call OI ratio is 0.19, and ATM IV is 214.8%. The stock ran up 19.6% over 5 days and 16.6% over 20 days, including +5.7% on Nov 3 and about +8% on Nov 4 on the Democratic midterm sweep. It is still -58.6% from its 52-week high. This is a crowded short with calls bid, so every negative below is shrunk for squeeze risk.

findings.finding: Cash generation is heavily back-end loaded against a guide the company has already cut once. Q1 2026 was -$31M ex-safe-harbor (against a Q1 guide of 'positive') and Q2 was +$45M, so H1 is about $14M. The FY guide of $200-375M therefore needs $186-361M in H2. In 2025, H2 delivered $295M (Q3 $108M, Q4 $187M) on 30,104 and 25,475 subscriber additions. Q2 2026 additions were 19,793 (-31% YoY) and management expects affiliate volume to fall more than 60% for the year. The market is holding the FY range, and a cut or a low-end landing at Q3 is the risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-05: EPS beat ($0.42 vs $0.23) and revenue beat, but the cash generation and ASV guide was cut and the stock went -10.58% close to close (more than -17% intraday per Investing.com). 2026-05-06: Q1 cash generation missed its own 'positive' guide while ASV beat its $850-950M guide at $1.08B, and the stock went +7.56%. 2026-02-26: -35.11% on the Q4 print with the initial 2026 guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is down about 26% since the August print and analysts cut targets through October (Jefferies $7, BMO $7.75, MS $10), so a low-end landing is expected. If an outright second cut were fully priced, the skew would be put-bid. Instead calls are bid by 28.5 points and the 5-day run-up is +19.6%, so the price leans to the range holding.
findings.independence: The quarterly 2025 split comes from a different document, the Q4 2025 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1469367/000162828026012266/q4258-kexhibit991.htm), and Q1 2026 from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001469367/000162828026031259/exhibit991q126.htm. Both are company documents of the same type. Goldman (2026-10-08) says the print must show direct installs growing more than 10% in H2 and must support the FY outlook: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/goldman-sachs-cut-sunrun-target-143616842.html

findings.finding: Q3 cost of capital rose after the guide was set. Jefferies (2026-10-09) cited a roughly 50bp rise in 7-year Treasury yields since the Aug 5 call as a headwind to the 2026 cash generation guide, and cut its target from $15 to $7. The 10-year closed at 5.24% on 2026-10-01 and has since eased to about 4.90% on 2026-11-04. That weighs on Q3 subscriber value and advance rates, while the late-October decline helps the Q4 and 2027 tone.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On Q2 2026 management named 'modestly higher' capital costs as one of three drivers of the guide cut, and the stock fell 10.58%. On 2026-11-02 RUN rose about 10% on falling Treasury yields (24/7 Wall St).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Jefferies called the impact 'within investor expectations', and the yield move is public. What is not visible is how much of it management passes through to the FY range. If it were fully priced, the Nov 2 rally on falling yields would not have needed to happen.
findings.independence: The yield levels come from https://statisticsoftheworld.com/news/2026-10-01 (10-year at 5.24% on Oct 1) and https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield (about 4.90% on Nov 4). This is macro-to-company transmission that the company has only confirmed in direction, on the Q2 call.

findings.finding: Counterparties that spoke after Sunrun's last report say demand is weak. Enphase (2026-10-27) said US residential permits were down about 35% YoY in Q3, that it sees no meaningful US recovery, and guided Q4 sell-through down 10%. SolarEdge (2026-11-04) guided Q4 revenue to $245-275M against $326.1M in Q3 and is cutting costs 'amid softer demand'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: RUN fell about 5% on 2026-10-28 alongside Enphase's -20% on its Q4 guide, then rebounded with the sector from Nov 2.
findings.why_not_priced: The SolarEdge guide came out the same morning (Nov 4) while RUN was up about 8% on the election. The Enphase read was traded on Oct 28. This is a proxy: both are hardware suppliers exposed to cash and loan buyers who lost the 25D credit, while Sunrun's lease and PPA model keeps 48E and its direct channel grew more than 10% YoY in June and July. The read-through is therefore weaker than the headline.
findings.independence: Enphase Q3 2026 release: https://newsroom.enphase.com/news-releases/news-release-details/enphase-energy-reports-financial-results-third-quarter-2026 and transcript summary https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-enphase-energy-q3-2026-profit-miss-sends-shares-lower-93CH-4977145. These are separate companies but the same industry proxy.

findings.finding: Crowded short into the print. 71.66M shares are short (32.4% of float, 8.75 days to cover, up from 70.71M), with a 25-delta skew of -28.5 vol points (calls bid) and put/call OI of 0.19. Any print that holds the FY range forces cover into a thin float.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-08-06: +32.3% and 2025-05-07: +15.0% on prints that were not cuts, with similarly heavy short interest (about 27-34% of float per aggregators). On 2026-11-04 the stock rose about 8% on the election with no company news.
findings.why_not_priced: The squeeze is partly under way: the 5-day run-up is +19.6%. If shorts had already covered, short interest would have fallen. Instead it rose between the last two settlements, which leaves the mechanism intact for a non-negative print.
findings.independence: Investing.com (2026-11-04) independently cites about 35% of float short: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-sunrun-stock-surging-today-93CH-4998496 . The baseline skew of -28.53 comes from the sealed option chain.

findings.finding: Management guided that direct-channel volume would return to YoY growth in Q3: monthly direct sales were up more than 10% YoY in June and July, the company expects to exit 2026 growing more than 10%, and the unit-margin pressure should largely ease by year-end. Direct is more than 85% of origination.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: an ASV beat against guide bought +7.56%. Q2 2026: an ASV result near the top of guide was outweighed by the FY cut (-10.58%).
findings.why_not_priced: This sits inside what the company already guided, so it is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect, and I sized it small. What is not known is whether the direct ramp delivered, which the October target cuts doubted.
findings.independence: Same call as finding 1's guide, different statement. It offsets finding 1 only in part: affiliate volume is still falling more than 60%, so total additions stay below Q3 2025's 30,104.

findings.finding: The sell-side bar came down into the print. Q3 EPS estimates fell more than 20% over two months (Investing.com). October target cuts: Jefferies $15 to $7, MS $15 to $10, BMO $10.50 to $7.75, Goldman $13 to $11, JPM $14 to $12, Barclays $14 to $12, Mizuho $18 to $15, Citi $16 to $14. The stock hit a 52-week low of $6.78 on Oct 19-20.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat lowered EPS bars by about 80% and still fell, because of the guide. RUN trades on guidance more than on EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: Lowered estimates are public. What matters is that the bar for 'not a cut' is now low, which makes a hold of the range a relief event. If the bar were still high, the skew would be put-bid.
findings.independence: The target cuts are listed in MarketBeat (2026-10-20): https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-sunrun-nasdaq-run-hits-new-12-month-low-after-analyst-downgrade-2026-10-20/ . A Zacks snippet relayed by solarcomplaint.com instead says the EPS consensus rose about 50% over the month, so the EPS bar itself is disputed.

findings.finding: Connecticut AG settlement (2026-10-23): Sunrun pays $300,000, must respond to covered complaints within 60 days, and per the page restitution carries no stated cap. This is a contract-review overhang that may come up on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction to a state settlement found.
findings.why_not_priced: It is small in dollars and there is no path to the guide unless restitution scales. I filed it at a fraction of its face value as a one-off.
findings.independence: None. The Investing.com preview also mentions the settlement as on investors' radar, but no second primary source was found.

findings.finding: ABS spreads kept tightening through Q3. The Aug 2026 $267M deal priced its A notes at a 200bp spread, 20bp tighter than April's 220bp and well inside the 240bp of July and September 2025. Q3 deals also included KBRA-rated Sunrun Prometheus 2026-1 (July, about $844M discounted solar asset balance) and Quintus 2026-2 (Aug 26, about $360M). This partly offsets the base-rate rise in Q3 cost of capital.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable. Q2's release cited tighter spreads alongside the guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: The deals are public, but the market has focused on base rates (the Jefferies note), not spreads. Market access is open and funding visible origination, so the sign is positive, but small. I found no public securitization in September or October, which leaves Q3 cash timing uncertain.
findings.independence: KBRA Quintus 2026-2 detail comes via https://solarcomplaint.com/research/sunrun-q3-2026-earnings and the KBRA listing https://www.kbra.com/publications/fdYqxzht . These are separate sources.

findings.finding: Democrats won both houses of Congress in the Nov 3 midterms. Barclays said this 'potentially reduces the risk of further political interference with renewable energy incentives', and RUN rose about 8% on Nov 4 on it. Management can frame 48E and storage durability on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: +5.7% on Nov 3 and about +8% on Nov 4. In Aug 2025 the stock rose about 10% on clearer Treasury tax-credit guidance (RBC upgrade).
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced in the sealed spot of $8.875. What may not be priced is management making it concrete for the 2027 tax-equity and FEOC outlook. A presidential veto still caps the legislative upside.

findings.finding: Insider selling in October was tax withholding on vested awards. CFO Abajian sold 16,734 shares and Jeanna Steele 10,042 on Oct 6 at $7.76. Insiders sold 118,719 shares (about $1.03M) in the quarter. This carries no directional information.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing to price. These are routine sales to cover tax withholding on vested awards.

outside_window.finding: Treasury must publish further FEOC safe-harbor tables and proposed regulations (prohibited foreign entity, material assistance) by 2026-12-31. These affect the 48E eligibility of 2027 lease and PPA systems.
October jobs report (Nov 6) and CPI (Nov 10) drive the rate path that sets Sunrun's capital costs. Both land after the exit window.

searched_and_found_nothing: Sunrun press releases Jul-Nov 2026 (investors.sunrun.com): only DPP/partnership PRs (SPAN, Voltus, Tesla dispatch, Puerto Rico DPP Nov 3). No financing 8-K, no pre-announcement, no guidance update.
No public Sunrun securitization press release in September or October 2026.
WARN notices in 2026: none found (warnfirehose and warntracker list nothing after 2024).
No consensus for Q3 Cash Generation or ASV found in any free source.
Freedom Forever: Chapter 11 filed Apr 2026, converted to Chapter 7 in Sep 2026. Already cited by management on the Aug 5 call, so nothing new.
FEOC/48E Treasury guidance: nothing new since Notice 2026-15 (Feb 2026), and nothing Sunrun-specific.
Nasdaq short-interest API returned 503. I used stockanalysis and Investing.com instead.

baseline_tension: The fundamentals I found (a back-end loaded cash guide, higher Q3 capital costs, weak peer demand) cut against the call-bid skew of -28.5 and the +19.6% 5-day run-up. With 32% of the float short, I could not say why the option market is wrong, so the negatives are shrunk and p_up sits at 49.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short, strong call skew against a negative sign): shrank the three negatives once each. Cash-guide back-end loading -2.0 to -1.5, rate headwind -1.0 to -0.7, peer demand read-through -1.0 to -0.7. p_up moved from 47 to 49.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the EPS bar is disputed across four sources, so I sized against the company's FY cash-generation and ASV guide instead and stated that in `bar`. No finding rests on EPS.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the ABS deals fund visible origination at tighter spreads, so that finding is signed positive and kept small.
Lesson 1 (reaction history): RUN trades on the guide, not the beat (the Q2 beat fell 10.6%), so the lowered-bar finding stays small.

Lessons 2, 5 and 9 left the rest standing: the CT settlement was already sized as a one-off, the peer read was already small and flagged as a proxy, and the direct-channel finding is already netted against affiliate decline.
